question: After source-declared MoE compiler/handle-domain coverage with full startup cost retained, does X retain complete-request advantage over ordinary full-stage F in a fresh finite arrival cohort?

warmup.state: Default non-injection/non-same-engine first-request warmup, full completion before measurement; per-policy expert cache retained, no measurement reset. Warmup requests/KV drain; completed request KV is naturally freed, prefix caching disabled.
warmup.jit_scope: Original single request warmup follows explicit compile-domain preparation. Validate actual measurement compiler events; do not infer all-runtime warmness.

experiment_unit: Four fresh engines, F/X/X/F, same new16 documents from unused second half of frozen input pool; two engines per mode, fixed order, descriptive pilot.
primary: first planned arrival to final completion of all16 requests
secondary: arrival-based per-request TTFT and completion latency
actual expert+KV bytes and CUDA peak allocated/reserved
entire subprocess wall including initialization,warmup,capture,finalize,IO and shutdown
accounting: Capture excludes prior warmup/setup and following finalization/shutdown; full subprocess wall retains all.
No cycle_complete or runtime GC observer in reused single-capture branch; memory trace retention stays until finalize, with cost retained.
Do not sum nested host/CUDA/apply spans into wall. Include actual preemption/recomputation, failures and every cell; no subtraction of warmup/observer/IO costs.

Clock arrivals are submitted between synchronous engine steps. Arrival lag is distinct from native queue waiting; cohort capture includes the initial arrival transient and final drain, but excludes engine startup. This finite cohort is not steady-state.
boundaries: Same frozen runtime and actual384expert slots/1GiBKV in F and X; proposed helper changes compiler state only.
All four cells and every output retained; timing-derived actual batching/route remains endogenous. No significance/quality/SLO or method GO from two repeats.
F is ordinary full-stage same-budget strong simple baseline, not optimized FreeToken reproduction.
Compiler-domain validation is distinct from performance. Any measurement compilation remains in time and marks that coverage assumption unfulfilled.
Latest queue owner must finish/release before this new group; shared advisory flock plus per-cell UUID/process queries. No kill or automatic waiter.

compiler_domain.position: After original engine initialization, before the sole 128->2 request warmup
compiler_domain.domain: M=1..160 x two actual BF16 MoE GEMM interfaces; F E64/global64/mapNone, X E384/global384/mapped. Enumerate full integer M domain with source exact config and alignment/EM rules.
compiler_domain.action: Compile-only warmup=True via original invoke helper and explicit CompiledKernel._init_handles; no expert/GPU kernel launch, pager ensure/LRU/KV or weight mutation.
compiler_domain.cache: Every fresh engine starts with its own empty private Triton disk cache. Other backend caches retain current environment and are not declared cold.
compiler_domain.coverage_rule: All source declared invocations complete; pager state unchanged; zero actual compiler_pipeline events during request measurement. Preserve any failure or miss as coverage failure, never delete or retry a cell.
compiler_domain.claim_boundary: Only this MoE Triton family compile/handles are covered, not all runtime paths. Monitor other compilers; full precompile/startup/memory cost retained. No subtraction or claim of full steady-state based on precompile alone.
compiler_domain.failure_policy: Stop after first completed cell whose coverage is false, keep its actual COMPLETE request status and all measurements; no automatic retry. Pending cells stay unrun.

implementation_fix: Read six pinned WispMoEState stats fields explicitly; CPU check uses actual slots. All original runtime, resources, sequence and workload preserved.
